findings.description: Header regeneration scope. SHEET-TAB-003's text says tabs 'shall be read-only and regenerated' with no distinction between header and data — and all three A-outputs read it literally: A1 clears the FULL used range starting at 'A1' (row 1, the header) and rewrites via a single values_update with no header/data split; A2's republish_tab calls client.write_values(..., &tab.header, &rows) on EVERY call, unconditionally re-sending the header; A3's own comment says 'row 0 = header' and its DeleteDimensionRange starts at start_index: 0 (the header row) followed by UpdateCells with fields: "*" — a full overwrite that includes the header every cycle. The real code does the opposite: sheets-view/src/lib.rs defines DATA_START_ROW = 2 and documents the header as 'Frozen; never rewritten on republish'; ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view (runtime/src/adapters.rs) only writes the header once, in the is_missing_tab bootstrap branch, and on every subsequent call touches only the range 'name'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z; testkit.rs's InMemorySheetsView enforces this as a hard, unconditional assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish") that panics in any build (not debug-only), and tests/tabs.rs's republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header exercises exactly this. All three B-outputs (B1, B2, B3) independently and precisely reconstruct this write-once/frozen-header mechanic. Neither the given SHEET-TAB-003 text nor any A-output anticipates that 'regenerated' excludes the header — a genuine spec-silent, code-enforced invariant that both directions converge on from opposite ends.

Basic-filter destruction is spec-claimed but nowhere implemented. SHEET-TAB-003 explicitly states 'a basic filter... is overwritten by design.' All three A-outputs took this literally enough to invent an explicit clearing step: A1 issues a ClearBasicFilterRequest via batch_update (treating an already-absent-filter error as success); A2 calls client.clear_basic_filter() when get_basic_filter() returns Some; A3 unconditionally appends a BatchUpdateRequest::ClearBasicFilter to its request batch. A grep of the entire crates/ tree (not just the four given files) turns up zero references to a Sheets basicFilter or FilterView object anywhere in the real implementation — ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view (adapters.rs) only ever calls self.api.update_range / self.api.ensure_sheet / self.api.read_range. Since a Sheets 'basic filter' is a persisted per-sheet object (range + criteria + sort) distinct from cell values, a values.update on the data range does not, by itself, clear or remove it — so the spec's specific claim that a basic filter is 'overwritten by design' has no corresponding code or test anywhere. None of the B-outputs surface this by name (there is nothing in the code to reconstruct), but B1/B2/B3's unanimous, precise description of the actual regeneration mechanism — a plain values overwrite of the data range only — is exactly what makes visible why that mechanism structurally cannot reach a basic-filter object. The two directions meet at the same underlying gap: the spec conflates a data-content concern (sort order, inserted rows — genuinely destroyed by full-range overwrite) with a metadata-object concern (a basic filter — not touched by that same mechanism) under one 'overwritten by design' clause.

Beyond SHEET-TAB-003's one-sentence scope, the real code (and all three B-outputs, near-verbatim) pins a cluster of mechanics the spec text never states: tail-truncation to the EXACT new row count on every republish (wholesale Vec replace in the fake, matching the trait doc's 'no leftover stale rows' contract); a full ten-tab workbook order (workbook_tab_order()) idempotently reasserted every republish regardless of per-tab outcome, superseding any manual tab reordering; a best-effort single-cell STALE banner at a fixed anchor (cell AA1) on a failed tab write, with the banner-write failure itself swallowed; an advisory write-lock acquired before any workbook mutation, whose failure yields a non-destructive published:false refusal with the stale set unchanged; per-tab failure isolation (one tab's batch_update_view failure doesn't block the others in the same republish call); and settle-pass price reads strictly serialized after all writes return. These are all real, verified-accurate (cross-checked each against lib.rs/adapters.rs/testkit.rs/tabs.rs), but likely land under separate EARS IDs (workbook layout, staleness/failure handling, marks settle-pass) not included in the SHEET-TAB-003 text given for this audit — flagged as legitimate code-side surplus relative to the one ID under test, with lower confidence that it constitutes drift IN SHEET-TAB-003 specifically rather than simply being out of this ID's scope.

notes: Scope: read all four named files in full (sheets-view/src/lib.rs, sheets-view/src/testkit.rs, sheets-view/tests/tabs.rs, runtime/src/adapters.rs) plus grepped the whole crates/ tree for 'filter' to confirm the basic-filter/FilterView absence wasn't just missing from the four given files. A1-A3's invented struct/trait shapes (CellValue, Row, ViewTab, GridRange, PublishError, etc.) are unanimous but self-labeled assumptions with zero textual basis in SHEET-TAB-003 — correctly treated as assumption artifacts, not findings. Likewise, all three A-outputs and all three B-outputs independently converge on rejecting a Sheets-ACL/ProtectedRange reading of 'read-only' (A: explicit assumption in each sketch that read-only means 'pipeline never reads edits back,' not access control; B: no ACL/protection code exists to reconstruct) — this is a genuinely coherent point (BD-COHERENT sub-finding), not drift, called out only to show the fleet isn't uniformly finding gaps everywhere.
